lane: wave-5 fleet-hygiene infra lane: the gate-bootstrap /etc/hosts remedy (operator queue item (a)); harness-side only - NO product change
hypothesis: The fleet-hygiene record 20260927-193330 established both pooled gate VMs as deterministically red on mcp_login::tests::worker_begin_login_persists_creds_and_unlocks_gating (the rust:1-bookworm image build intermittently ships a 59-NUL-byte /etc/hosts; the files leg is unparseable, getent hosts localhost fails rc=2, the DNS fallback NXDOMAINs the bare single-label name, getaddrinfo returns EAI_NONAME). The documented standing remedy - an /etc/hosts overwrite at gate VM claim/bootstrap with a probe assertion - should turn both pooled slots' deterministic reds green with NO product change, and be a no-op on well-formed fresh VMs.
approach:
fleet_pipeline v1.4.5 -> v1.4.6 (module /home/ubuntu/.prime/agent/fleet-tools/fleet_pipeline.py, version-controlled at /home/ubuntu/lane-worktrees/fleet-tools): (1) new HOSTS_GUARD constant run via the VM claim path on BOTH _op_gate and _op_review, right after kill-verify-claim and BEFORE any test run (also covers spec['vm'] triage-VM gates, which skip the pool claim but hit the same call site); (2) guard semantics: probe getent hosts localhost + an od-based NUL-byte check; on a broken file OVERWRITE (never append - appending after NUL padding stays unparseable, proven 2026-09-23) with the known-good shape '127.0.0.1	localhost
::1	localhost ip6-localhost ip6-loopback
192.0.2.1	prime.internal
' (the fresh-VM well-formed shape per the hygiene record, plus the task-directed ::1 line), probe-assert getent after the write, emit a clear HOSTS_REPAIR log line, and keep a VM-side hosts_corrupt_<tag>.log snapshot of the pre-repair file; well-formed files are untouched (HOSTS_OK no-op); (3) every gate/review verdict now carries hosts_guard: OK|REPAIRED and a guard failure RED_SETUPs ('localhost must resolve before any test runs'); (4) gate + review harness skill entries re-registered with the guard note (register_skills, v1.4.6). Infra repairs en route: the fleet-tools VC repo at /home/ubuntu/lane-worktrees/fleet-tools was GONE (deleted at some point) - re-seeded from the live module with a byte-identical v1.4.5 baseline commit 106f60f (sha256 524f5130d4eab5b771cb5ff87717f6c8dd6afd766d1ac5ca0b857dd226b8cef) then the fix commit d9d45af, copy-to-live sha-verified (e1c3e3775c3f9ff95c7a44cee9f0a13e31fd24f634b97362945a0cdd3ed2b522); the missing kernel-venv fleet_pipeline.pth (the import-by-name contract was broken after a venv rebuild) restored.
